punchline: During the thirteen days of the Cuban Missile Crisis, Kennedy filled a notepad with sailboats and key words while his advisers argued for force.
thirty_sec: In 1962 the Soviets put missiles in Cuba, and Kennedy's advisers wanted a military answer. He had read The Guns of August, about leaders who stumbled into a war, so he kept asking what the other side would do after each move. He drew sailboats and key words on a notepad, chose a naval blockade over an attack, and Khrushchev withdrew the missiles. Ryan Holiday holds it up as stillness under pressure.
